title: Apply a list of operations in order
prompt: Start with the supplied integer and apply each operation once, from left to right. Return the final value. An empty operation list returns the starting value. Test inputs stay within int range.
signature: int applyAll(int start, const std::vector<std::function<int(int)>>& operations)
driver: int main(){int n;if(!(std::cin>>n))return 2;std::cout<<applyAll(n,{[](int x){return x+2;},[](int x){return x*3;}})<<"\n";}

tests.label: Order matters
tests.hint: Use the previous result as the next input.

tests.label: One operation
tests.hint: Invoke a supplied function rather than returning it.

tests.label: Called once each
tests.expression: ([]{int calls=0;int value=applyAll(1,{[&](int x){++calls;return x+1;},[&](int x){++calls;return x*2;}});return value==4&&calls==2;})()
tests.hint: Do not repeat a callback to inspect its result.

hints: An operation can be called like a normal function: operation(current).
const auto& borrows each stored function object.
explanation: This is a small pipeline: each stage receives the output of the stage before it. The loop separates the order of work from the details of each operation.
